head_commit.message:
pm-270/t-1605: Anchor the leftover-child check and bound the deploy step at 12 minutes

The contract checks re-run on HEAD 3ae76a4 (Linux, GNU timeout 9.4) found two failures:
- vercel-deploy.test.sh reported 31/33. `pgrep -f "sleep 6011"` matched any
  process whose command line quotes that text (here the agent's own), and
  `pgrep -x sleep` showed no real leftover. It is now anchored to the fake's
  argv, `^sleep 6011$`. Negative control: with bounded() mutated to
  `timeout --foreground`, both child checks fail again.
- The wiring check required timeout-minutes: 12 in production. ec59663
  (pm-249/t-1569) raised the job to 18 for verify-deploy's live e2e. The job
  stays at 18, and "Deploy and verify the served sha" gets its own 12-minute
  step budget, so a stall names the deploy step.

vercel-deploy.sh is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

pm-257/t-1607: Build bounded ghost rooms and Worker adapter

Add the ink-ghosts transport: shared protocol, upgrade policy and pure room
(two rooms, exact origins, 24-socket cap, 128-byte frames, 15/s token bucket
over every attempt, five invalid frames then 1008), a hibernating GhostRoom
Durable Object Worker in its own locked package (typecheck, test:local in

deploy --dry-run, /version fingerprint), and a dependency-free local fake
that runs the same contract cases. No storage, logs, cookies, IP or UA.

workflow_runs.display_title: pm-270/t-1605: Bound the Vercel production deploy and assert the serv…

head_commit.message:
pm-270/t-1605: Bound the Vercel production deploy and assert the served sha

Run 40311256064's blocking `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod` hung 850 s
until the 15-minute job timeout, with no public state and the health
check skipped; that check only asserted 200.

scripts/vercel-deploy.sh replaces the deploy and health steps:
- upload with --no-wait under a 300 s bound; retry once only on a fast
  failure with no deployment URL, never after a timeout or once a URL exists
- `vercel inspect <url> --wait --timeout 6m --logs` under a 420 s bound;
  on failure re-read the state and print ::error title=vercel deploy::<state> <url>
- /api/health (HEALTH_URL) must report "sha":"$GITHUB_SHA"
- bounds use GNU timeout (process group), a perl fallback on macOS

scripts/vercel-deploy.test.sh drives it with a fake npx: 25 checks
including a hanging upload failing in 4 s with one deploy call and no
leftover child, a hanging inspect printing "Building after 2s <url>",
a healthy deploy, and a health body for another sha failing. It runs in
the checks job; production timeout-minutes goes 15 -> 12.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

workflow_runs.display_title: pm-258/t-1564: Annotate failed E2E tests in CI and add a flowing-cloc…

head_commit.message:
pm-258/t-1564: Annotate failed E2E tests in CI and add a flowing-clock control to Kame's hold threshold

CI job logs need a token, but check-run annotations and the step
summary do not. Under GitHub Actions, scripts/e2e.mjs adds
scripts/e2e-annotate.mjs beside TAP, so each failed test becomes an
::error annotation (file, line, assertion) and a step summary section.
The CI E2E step keeps next start's log, adds its tail and the
build/node/chrome identity to the summary on failure, and exits with
the suite's own status. lib/e2e-runner.test.ts covers the reporter,
with outside-Actions as the negative control, and pins the workflow
step.

e2e/kame.test.ts:90 failed in 2 of 3 full E2E runs in an Ubuntu 24.04
container. Playwright's installed clock flows with real time until
pauseAt(), so the round trips around runFor(499) carried it past
PET_MS. 9ddd084 (pm-259/t-1583) landed the same pause concurrently,
so this commit keeps that pause and adds only the negative control:
on a resumed clock, 50 real ms beside the same runFor(499) already
pets Kame.
